subject: Computer Networking
title: Self-Hosted vs Cloud Email
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Self-Hosted vs Cloud Email.

hook.text: Run your own email server or pay Google? The choice seems simple, but the trade-offs are deep.

buildup.text: Self-hosting gives full control: your data, your rules, your privacy. No third party reads your mail.

discovery.text: But maintaining deliverability alone is a full-time job. One misconfigured SPF record and you're blocklisted.

twist.text: Cloud providers handle spam filtering, uptime, and security patches. You trade control for convenience.

climax.text: Some run hybrid setups: cloud for delivery infrastructure, self-hosted for storage and encryption.

punchline.text: Self-host for control. Cloud for convenience. Hybrid for both.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge of self-hosting email?
options: The cost of electricity for the server
Finding an email client that supports self-hosted servers

details.summary: Self-hosted email gives full control over data but requires maintaining servers, security updates, spam filtering, and deliverability. Cloud email services like Gmail and Outlook handle all of this. The trade-off is between privacy and control versus convenience and reliability.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing between self-hosted and cloud email involves fundamental trade-offs in control, privacy, cost, and reliability. Most organizations choose cloud because email operations are complex.
takeaways: Self-hosted gives control but demands ongoing maintenance
Cloud services handle spam, security, and deliverability
Most organizations migrate to cloud for reliability and cost

faq.question: Why is self-hosting email so difficult?
faq.answer: Maintaining deliverability requires proper authentication, IP reputation management, and constant spam filter tuning. Security patches must be applied immediately. Backup and redundancy require additional infrastructure.

faq.question: When does self-hosted email still make sense?
faq.answer: Organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, those in heavily regulated industries, and privacy-focused entities may need self-hosted email. Some governments require domestic email infrastructure. The trade-off is justified when regulatory compliance mandates full data control.
